Cross-Era Net Flux

Source: R/dp-crossera.R
dp_flux.Rd

Usage

dp_flux(
  resistance,
  present,
  future,
  source_threshold = 0.01,
  resistance_is = "resistances",
  direction = TRUE
)

Arguments

resistance

A terra::SpatRaster or file path: the resistance (or conductance) surface. Or a circuit from dp_circuit(), to reuse its factorization.

present, future

terra::SpatRasters or file paths on the same grid as resistance: present and future source strength, e.g. habitat suitability. NA counts as 0.

source_threshold

Numeric. Cells with source strength below this are not sources (or sinks). Default 0.01.

resistance_is

Character. Whether resistance holds "resistances" (default) or "conductances". Ignored for a circuit.

direction

Logical. Also return the components of net flow. Default TRUE.

Value

A terra::SpatRaster with layers:

current

Half the sum of absolute current over a cell's links, as in Circuitscape's current maps (without the injection term).

flow_x, flow_y

(with direction) Net flow through the cell towards the east and the north, in grid directions: half the sum over the cell's links of the current along the link times its unit direction.

Attribute "imbalance" (see Details).

Details

Maps the net flow of a range shift: present habitat injects current and future habitat withdraws it, in fixed amounts, in one solve. The result is signed, so it has direction.

The injection is \(b = p / \sum p - f / \sum f\), with \(p\) and \(f\) the present and future source strengths: one unit enters at present habitat and leaves at future habitat, wherever it has to travel. This is the minimum-energy flow that turns the present distribution into the future one. Only the cell totals matter, not which present cell pairs with which future cell, so there is no dispersal limit; show results beside a dispersal-limited map such as dp_pathways(). Where present and future habitat coincide, injection and withdrawal cancel, so net flux mostly measures movement from lost to gained habitat.

Withdrawals are fixed, not grounds: each future cell takes its share however far away it is. (With grounds, as in cs_advanced(), current drains into the nearest future habitat instead.)

Current can't cross NA cells, so the flow must balance within each group of connected cells (component). Within a component holding present share \(P_c\) and future share \(F_c\) of the totals, both are scaled to \((P_c + F_c)/2\); components with no present or no future habitat carry no flow. The share that would have had to move between components, \(\sum_c |P_c - F_c| / 2\), is returned as the "imbalance" attribute, with a warning if it exceeds 1%.

See also

dp_pathways(), cs_advanced()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # circuitscaper::cs_julia_available(circuitscape = FALSE)
resistance <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata/resistance.tif",
                                      package = "circuitscaper"))
present <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata/source.tif", package = "circuitscaper"))
future <- terra::flip(present, "horizontal")
result <- dp_flux(resistance, present, future)
terra::plot(result)
DONTSHOW({JuliaConnectoR::stopJulia()})
}
